title: RAW UNREVIEWED: repeat a complete predicate head for an explicitly counted shared-argument instruction
summary: A narrow invented extension of the existing productive teaching grammar lets an explicitly supplied ITER(n,P,args) write the complete self-delimiting predicate stem P exactly n times in one group, then write its arguments once. This pays an exact number of ordered invocations with shared argument bindings. It does not automatically merge repeated words, assign a plural meaning to doubling, or translate any native form. The repetition idea has explicit older predecessors; the proposed addition is this complete forward module and its scope contract.

base_contract.unchanged: Retain the old29 root meanings and two-sign teaching table,17 unary tags, productive nominal constructors, eight grammatical references, LIT spelling, QUOTE0..3 arity, source normalization, argument order, statement-start m and all old non-ITER expressions. No raw946 name cache is imported. This card does not alter any existing file or claim that1175's frozen writer has changed.
base_contract.domain: The existing finite expressions, plus the restricted ITER expressions below. The input is an explicitly interpreted message in this artificial teaching language, not automatically analyzed historical prose. The old a-z restriction on open names remains. Unsupported characters, source structures or semantic interpretations must be reported, not normalized away.
base_contract.new_operator: ITER(n,P(A1,...,Aa)), integer n>=2, means one counted instruction or procedure expression containing exactly n successive complete invocations of P with the same once-bound argument values. The operator must be explicitly present in the input message. It is not inferred from two equal neighboring words, source spelling similarity, native BB, or a desire to shorten the text.
base_contract.argument_binding: Bind the a written argument expressions once for this ITER occurrence, in their written order, then reuse those a slots for each invocation. Equivalently: LET(v1=A1,...,va=Aa; STEP(P,v1,...,va) repeated n times). LET/STEP here explain the fixed grammar semantics; they are not extra hidden source data or free selectable meanings. An indefinite argument introduces its referent once for the counted instruction. An unresolved pronoun remains one unresolved shared slot; it is not identified with a particular ingredient by this writer. Re-evaluating an indefinite expression to introduce a new portion on every repetition is a DIFFERENT input and is not represented by this operator.
base_contract.semantic_limit: An iteration requests or denotes ordered applications, not a guaranteed change in the final physical state, increased intensity, plural objects, restoration of an earlier state, or a repeated assertion for emphasis. An idempotent operation still has n declared invocation positions. Physical executability and a quoted action's ordinary lexical meaning are not proved by the notation.

eligible_heads_and_arguments.known_arity: Keep each listed head's existing arity and ordered roles: MAKE2, CHOP1, TAKE1, PUT2, SET2, STIR1, POUR2, CUT1. No special argument deletion is introduced.
eligible_heads_and_arguments.open_heads: QUOTE0:name, QUOTE1:name, QUOTE2:name and QUOTE3:name, with a nonempty a-z name, may be used as literal calls to an unfamiliar procedure. ITER itself states that the quoted name is used as a procedure call; it does not supply the procedure's lexical meaning. The written QUOTE arity stays part of the complete repeated head. A noun or property is not silently reinterpreted as an action merely because its name could be spelled.
eligible_heads_and_arguments.nominal_argument_domain: Each Ai is a finite nominal expression built from the old zero-arity nominal roots, old reference values or LIT names; ORIGIN/KIND combine two such expressions and YOUNG one; DEF,INDEF,PLURAL,SMALL,HARD,GOOD,FROM,IN,ON may wrap such an expression. These are the existing constructor/tag meanings. This domain excludes executable action subtrees inside an argument, so spelling one argument does not hide an uncounted procedure to be re-executed.
eligible_heads_and_arguments.excluded_heads: No bare BUILD sign, APPLY/REL composite head, nominal root, reference value, UNTIL/AFTER/JOIN/LIKE/IDENTITY relation head, BOIL/BECOME state/inception head or modified inner predicate becomes repeatable by this module. A future extension would be a changed contract. In particular existing PLURAL remains explicitly marked and is not replaced by nominal doubling.
eligible_heads_and_arguments.scope: The repeated head contains only P, including a quoted name and arity where applicable. Existing unary tags attached to its written group scope OUTSIDE ITER. Thus NOT(ITER(2,P(args))) differs from ITER(2,NOT(P(args))); the latter is outside this module's domain. Conditions or other wrappers in the surrounding old tree retain their written scope. If their practical interpretation conflicts with completing n invocations, report that input conflict rather than silently changing the count or moving the wrapper.
eligible_heads_and_arguments.nesting: Direct nested iteration ITER(m,ITER(n,P(...))) is outside the accepted domain. Do not multiply counts or flatten it automatically. A count of1 must be supplied as ordinary P; zero/negative counts are rejected, not erased. No maximum count is fitted; large counts pay correspondingly large written heads.

complete_head_encoding.known_B: For a listed known head P, B is its exact old two-working-sign root code. These heads start with old lexical head signs and their second sign is one of a,o,e,i. No second private dictionary is added.
complete_head_encoding.open_B: For QUOTEa:name, B is e + arity_selector[a] + l + spell(name) + r, with arity_selectors a,o,e,i for0..3. This is the unchanged old QUOTE head. The a-s source letters use the old19 one-sign values; t-z use q plus the first seven selectors. Raw r and y are absent from spell(name), so the literal end is explicit. All these entries remain part of the learner's old paid table.
complete_head_encoding.prefix_boundary: The eligible known two-sign heads have different initial signs from e. Open heads start e, have one fixed arity selector and one nonempty l...r literal. Hence the eligible complete B codes are prefix-free under the stipulated22-working-sign inventory. A longer spelling of an unknown name is not split on an accidental repeated substring.
complete_head_encoding.native_limit: These are inherited artificial teaching values, not an identified native alphabet or assignments to ol,olol,dal,daldy. The teaching key is not nominated as a fitting native key. A native application would need its own justified sign/group and lexical binding; no global renaming is selected here.

writer: Apply only the old declared source normalizations. Do not infer a new ITER from neighboring identical subtrees or words. If normalization would turn the proposed P into an ineligible composite such as APPLY, reject that ITER input rather than rename it to evade the restriction.
As in the old writer, peel the unary tag chain of the expression in outer-to-inner order. If the remaining expression is ordinary, use the old word rule unchanged.

If it is ITER(n,P(A1,...,Aa)), verify the eligible head, its exact arity and nominal argument domain. Form the one complete B. Write B concatenated with itself n times in one visible group, followed by the old y plus tag chain if nonempty.

Emit the a arguments once, in their old prefix-tree order and old group encoding. No argument is inferred from a previous instruction or a source-side table. Their full spelling, grammar and boundaries remain written.

The old statement-start m is still written once on a statement's first group, outside the repeated B. It is not part of the repeated stem. Ordinary physical line wraps do not reset or change anything.
reader: Use the existing statement marker and group boundaries. Remove a statement-start m only where the existing grammar licenses it; it is not an optional root fragment or a reset for arbitrary interior words.
Parse the first core as before. If its head is ineligible, use the complete old one-core-plus-tags rule; this includes all legitimate old bare BUILD forms.

For an eligible first B, remember its complete working-sign sequence and parse further eligible complete heads until the group's end or the old y tag boundary. Every further head must be exactly the same B, with the same quoted spelling and arity if present. Reject a different second head or a malformed/partial copy.
One B reconstructs the old predicate template. n>=2 reconstructs ITER(n,that one predicate template). The template contains only a pending argument slots, not n*a slots.

Read the old tags and wrap them outside that result in the old scope order. Read/fill exactly the a following argument expressions once and check the nominal domain for ITER. The decoded message therefore contains the explicit count, the original predicate and its complete ordered argument expressions.

To understand or execute ITER, retain these a values for the current counted instruction and invoke P n times in sequence. No state is inherited from an unrecorded earlier command. The next independently written instruction receives its own argument evaluation.
why_this_has_B_and_BB: For every eligible complete B, the head groups B and BB are legal when no outer unary tag is attached. Both can occur as interior expression groups under the unchanged prefix-tree message grammar; at a statement beginning the separately paid m remains. BB is a derived iteration head, not a second independent lexical meaning. A learner may recognize BB as a whole, but its definition must remain ITER(2,B) with the same arity, arguments and state effects. This is a construction property, not a native interpretation.

invented_demonstrations.explanation: The brackets/groups are teaching typography. The inherited artificial values say stir the named broth once versus invoke the same stirring instruction twice, sharing its one written broth argument. m and the DO tag are each paid once outside the duplicated complete head. No Voynich group is translated by this example.

invented_demonstrations.head: Let B be exactly the old QUOTE2:zelmor head, including e, the arity2 selector, the complete spelled name and r. Write BB; then write both complete nominal arguments once in order.
invented_demonstrations.readback: Two invocations of the unfamiliar two-place procedure zelmor, with the same once-bound nava argument and the same in-peru argument. All three invented names remain literal and unexplained. No procedure meaning, material identity or place is inferred. The reader can recover the exact count, spelling, arity and scope even without knowing what the procedure does.

invented_demonstrations.contrast: DO(ITER(2,TAKE(INDEF(LIT:nava)))) versus two separate DO(TAKE(INDEF(LIT:nava))) instructions
invented_demonstrations.meaning: The ITER introduces its one indefinite argument once and reuses it for two invocations. The two separately written instructions each have their own indefinite introduction. The writer does not fuse them because their names or outer word forms happen to match. This is the declared argument-binding distinction, not a claim about real recipe portions.

invented_demonstrations.required_handling: Keep all three ordered instructions in the first case and both different argument expressions in the second. Neither is represented by ITER(2,P(x)). A source statement asking for a fresh object at every repetition is likewise outside this shared-binding shorthand; it cannot borrow the once-bound reading.

invented_demonstrations.whole_word_repetition: Two equal old nominal argument expressions still emit equal neighboring groups wherever the old arity grammar places them next to each other. Two separately written equal instructions remain separate and can have identical group sequences. No compulsory merging of equal neighboring groups is introduced.

cost_and_human_work.inherited: All old29 root values, arities,17 tags, productive/reference rules and26 letter mappings remain paid. The ordinary source-language knowledge behind unknown names is not learned for free from QUOTE. There is no claim that the entire old teaching system consists of one simple new rule.
cost_and_human_work.additional: Learn one exact positive-count operator, the eligible head category, the once-bound shared-argument scope, outside-tag scope, and the rejection of heterogeneous, partial or nested head repetition. A scribe copies the full visible B n times and tallies n; a reader recognizes its fixed boundary and counts the copies.
cost_and_human_work.written: If B costs b working signs, its ITER head costs n*b before unchanged outer tags and statement prefix. Arguments cost their complete old spelling once. An unfamiliar quoted head repeats its full spelling n times, so unknown verbs may become very long. There is no extra hidden count code and no zero-cost omitted name.
cost_and_human_work.memory: The current B, an integer tally and at most three current argument values for an open head (at most two for the known heads). Argument descriptions may themselves be long; the reader can reread the current instruction, but this is real work, not a constant-bit memory claim. No growing history, permanent new-word dictionary or prior-word state is used.
cost_and_human_work.limit: This proposal does not claim to repair1175's spelling cost, meet word-frequency or length distributions, or explain q-to-o and common native endings. Large counts, long open names and different arguments are immediate practical obstacles.

minimal_falsifiers_and_boundaries: A claimed decode of BB with different second predicate, different second argument bindings, a hidden per-iteration fresh portion, or an unpriced internal condition violates the frozen rule.

A candidate demanding BB as an independent unrelated root conflicts with this module unless a separately written independent literal name represents that different concept. Learning the larger BB spelling is allowed only with its unchanged expansion, as1201 requires.

A proposed universal noun-plural interpretation is outside the contract. Nested nominal ORIGIN/KIND terms retain their old explicit parser and PLURAL remains marked; no repeated nominal substring is consumed as an iteration.

BdyBdy is not BBdy. Under this module outer tags follow the entire repeated head once; repeating an already modified complete instruction is a different source scope and cannot be silently assigned this spelling.
Known identical whole-word neighbors and y/r/l endings are retained obligations, not passed native checks. No f45r.10 parse, native source frame, word meaning or native marker is supplied here.

The smallest useful future review is a manual complete scope/argument contrast under this frozen contract. Merely showing that a counter can count copies would add no manuscript evidence and does not justify a large implementation.

predecessors.relation: Read after the complete raw draft, before registry submission. The unchanged old B6 word grammar cannot support the short whole-word square under any global working-sign bijection, including its bare BUILD and statement-prefix allowances. This proposed repetition rule is an actual prospective grammar change, not a renamed table or a repair to1214's recorded outcome. Changed formal expressibility alone is not native fit, selected morphology or source-cost success.

Already proposes free noun plurality/action repetition versus package nesting in an old native-card interpretation. Those native values and historical claims are not adopted. Repetition itself is not a new idea; this card instead fixes an input operator, open names, head parser, arity, explicit scope and bound arguments for an invented forward channel.

The old count voice already preserves two adjacent action slots and refuses to collapse interrupted order.575 distinguishes same-root repeats, different-root voice collisions and scope pairs;579 retains outer/inner scope rather than converting it to a count. These exact cautions remain. They are not a complete open-name forward ITER code or native confirmation of this new contract.

Whole-word repetition can be noun reprise, repeated predicate or clause boundary. No universal count value follows. This source-control rule is deliberately not selected from native adjacent doublets and supplies no old glossary value.
DUP/ECHO/SINGLE expansions of the fixed qoqo family lacked suitable comparison capacity and no meaning was selected. Those outcomes remain; no qo or qoqo value is used by this module.

1200 establishes only formal families and the B/BB parse obligation.1201 already proves that learned larger chunks may share one expanded message. This proposal neither rediscovers that theorem nor equates native joined/split forms: it adds a narrowly defined semantic shared-argument instruction contract.

The old complete29-root writer remains stopped for its declared spelling costs. This new untested operator pays additional repeated head spelling and does not recover missing short vocabulary. No old output, source interpretation or threshold is revised.
